blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Non-Constitutional bodies are organizations not explicitly mentioned in the Constitution of India.
Statutory bodies are created by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature (e.g., NHRC, CVC, CIC, NGT).
Non-Statutory (Executive) bodies are established by an executive resolution or Cabinet order without legislative enactment (e.g., NITI Aayog).
Constitutional bodies derive power directly from constitutional articles, whereas non-constitutional bodies derive power from statutes or executive mandates.
Reforms are continuously required to ensure operational autonomy, adequate funding, and functional efficiency for these bodies.

blocks.content: Non-Constitutional Bodies are those institutions which are not mentioned in the Constitution of India.
They are created either by an Act of Parliament or by an executive order of the government.
These bodies assist the government in administration, regulation, policy implementation, and welfare activities.
Although they do not derive their authority from the Constitution, they play a very important role in governance.
The government alone cannot efficiently handle all administrative and developmental responsibilities.
Therefore, Non-Constitutional Bodies are created to:

items:
• Provide expert knowledge
  • Reduce administrative burden
  • Improve efficiency
  • Implement welfare schemes
  • Ensure specialization in governance

blocks.content: Non-Constitutional Bodies are broadly classified into:
Statutory Bodies are created by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature. Characteristics:

items:
• Have legal backing
  • Defined powers and functions
  • Can be abolished or modified only by law
  • More authoritative than non-statutory bodies
Can be abolished or modified only by law

• National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
  • National Commission for Women (NCW)
  • Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)
  • Central Information Commission (CIC)
  • National Green Tribunal (NGT)
  • National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission

blocks.content: The NHRC was established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act. Composition:

items:
• Chairperson (former Chief Justice of India)
  • Judicial and non-judicial members

• Protection of human rights
  • Inquiry into violations
  • Recommendations to government
  • Awareness and promotion of human rights
Awareness and promotion of human rights

blocks.content: The CVC was established in 1964 and given statutory status in 2003. Functions:

items:
• Supervision of vigilance administration
  • Prevention of corruption
  • Supervision over CBI in corruption cases
Supervision over CBI in corruption cases

blocks.content: The CIC was established under the Right to Information Act, 2005. Functions:

items:
• Hearing RTI appeals
  • Ensuring transparency
  • Enforcing citizens’ right to information

blocks.content: The NGT was established in 2010 for environmental protection. Functions:

rows: Established by an Act of Parliament or State Legislature
Established by a Cabinet Resolution or Executive Order
Specific Statute / Law passed by the legislature
Requires an amendment or repeal of the statute in Parliament
Can be altered or abolished directly by an executive order
NITI Aayog, Law Commission of India

blocks.content: Non-Statutory Bodies are created by executive orders or resolutions. They do not have legal backing and can be dissolved easily.They mainly function as advisory or coordinating bodies.

items:
• NITI Aayog
  • National Development Council
  • Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI)
  • National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)

blocks.content: NITI Aayog was established in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission. Functions:

items:
• Policy formulation
  • Cooperative federalism
  • Long-term development planning
  • Monitoring implementation of schemes

blocks.content: DIFFERENCE BETWEEN STATUTORY AND NON-STATUTORY BODIES

items:
• Created by executive order
  • No legal backing
  • Advisory in nature

blocks.content: DIFFERENCE BETWEEN CONSTITUTIONAL AND NON-CONSTITUTIONAL BODIES

items:
• Created by law or executive action
  • Can be abolished easily
  • Limited autonomy
Created by law or executive action
NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional, non-statutory body created by a Cabinet resolution, replacing the Planning Commission.
NHRC (Protection of Human Rights Act 1993), CVC (CVC Act 2003), CIC (RTI Act 2005), and NGT (NGT Act 2010) are statutory bodies created by specific Acts of Parliament.
Exams frequently test the distinction between Constitutional bodies (e.g., UPSC, Election Commission) and Statutory/Non-Constitutional bodies.

• Assist government in governance
  • Improve administrative efficiency
  • Provide expert advice
  • Support policy implementation
  • Help in service delivery

• Lack of constitutional protection
  • Political interference
  • Overlapping functions
  • Limited enforcement powers

• Greater functional autonomy
  • Transparent appointments
  • Clear jurisdiction
  • Strengthening accountability mechanisms

blocks.content: Non-Constitutional Bodies play a crucial role in the governance system of India.
Though they lack constitutional status, their contribution to administration, development, and regulation is significant.
Strengthening these institutions will enhance efficiency, transparency, and good governance.
